Substantial substitute hosting during her mother’s illness, especially Monroe’s second term. Range describes that term, not uninterrupted service.

Miller Center explicitly identifies Polly as a substitute when Patsy could not host, before her death in 1804. Dates of those particular duties are not given. Monticello biography was inaccessible; no continuous tenure or exact season invented.

LOC explicitly identifies her as White House hostess; WHHA describes substantial social and administrative responsibilities after Ellen’s death, alongside Margaret Wilson. Dates describe the widower interval rather than an exclusive appointment; she remained in the household afterward.

questions: Hostess scope is evidence-based and extensible; WHHA explicitly says other hostesses may exist. New names require evidence of substantial substitute duties, not merely event attendance.
Mary Cleveland Hoyt: establish exact dates and extent of hosting; inclusion is supported by WHHA scholarship, not a fully dated biography.
Reconcile Jackson household shared duties and interruptions; the NPS and WHHA index start/end years differ.
Taft substitutes and Pierce substitutes: refine individual intermittent service ranges without inventing exact dates.
Maria Jefferson Eppes: substantial substitute role confirmed by Miller Center; establish dates of particular hosting duties. Monticello biography retrieval failed, so service dates remain unknown.

Harrison administration candidates: assess whether Jane Irwin Findlay’s help with two receptions and Anna Tuthill Harrison Taylor’s reported co-hosting meet the substantial-role threshold. WHHA/Smithsonian support Findlay’s assistance, but further institutional evidence is needed before adding full roster identities. These are unresolved inclusion candidates, not missing published profiles.
